definitions.explanation: An area where people live, as opposed to wilderness or uninhabited mountain/forest areas. Often used when describing remote locations in relation to human settlements.

examples.japanese: {人里|ひとざと}{離|はな}れた{場所|ばしょ}に{住|す}んでいる。
examples.english: I live in a place far from human habitation.

examples.japanese: {熊|くま}が{人里|ひとざと}に{下|お}りてきた。
examples.english: A bear came down to the inhabited area.

examples.japanese: {冬|ふゆ}になると{鹿|しか}が{食|た}べ{物|もの}を{求|もと}めて{人里|ひとざと}に{近|ちか}づくことがある。
examples.english: In winter, deer sometimes approach human settlements in search of food.

notes:
USAGE:
{人里|ひとざと} is most commonly used in the expression {人里|ひとざと}{離|はな}れた (far from human habitation), describing remote or secluded locations. It is also frequently used in nature and wildlife contexts when animals approach populated areas.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {人里|ひとざと}{離|はな}れた: remote, far from settlements
- {人里|ひとざと}に{近|ちか}い: near inhabited areas
- {人里|ひとざと}に{下|お}りる: to come down to human settlements (of animals)
- {人里|ひとざと}から{遠|とお}い: far from inhabited areas
